content: Torsemide is a diuretic, commonly referred to as a water pill, that is prescribed to alleviate swelling and fluid retention caused by conditions such as heart or liver disease. It is also used to manage high blood pressure. This medication works by prompting the kidneys to excrete excess water and salt through urine. In some cases, torsemide may be prescribed for other purposes; consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Torsemide is available in tablet form and is typically taken orally once a day in the morning. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and ask your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take torsemide exactly as directed. Do not take more or less of it, or take it more frequently than prescribed. While torsemide helps control high blood pressure, it does not cure the condition. Continue taking torsemide even if you feel well, and do not stop taking it without consulting your doctor. Before starting torsemide, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to torsemide, sulfa drugs, or any other medications. Additionally, disclose all other medications, supplements, or vitamins you are taking, as certain drugs may interact with torsemide. Notify your doctor if you have a history of diabetes, gout, or kidney or liver disease. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. Do not breastfeed while taking this medication. If you become pregnant while on torsemide, contact your doctor immediately. If you are scheduled for surgery, including dental procedures, inform your healthcare provider that you are taking torsemide. Follow your doctor’s dietary recommendations while on torsemide. Your doctor may advise you to include potassium-rich foods, such as bananas, prunes, raisins, and orange juice, in your diet. If you miss a dose of torsemide, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Frequent urination is a common side effect of torsemide and may last up to six hours after taking a dose. This effect typically diminishes after a few weeks of use. Notify your doctor if you experience severe or persistent symptoms such as muscle cramps, weakness, dizziness, faintness, fatigue, headache, confusion, thirst, upset stomach, or vomiting. If you experience serious side effects, such as rapid and excessive weight loss or vomiting blood, contact your doctor immediately. Serious side effects can also be reported to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store torsemide in its original container, tightly sealed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (do not store it in the bathroom). Dispose of expired or unneeded medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. In case of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory for regular monitoring. Your blood pressure should be checked regularly, and occasional blood tests may be required. Do not share your medication with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist.
